items.spec:
Repo ../WowAddonStandards (default branch master, detect it with `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`). Create branch feat/2026-10-24-keybinds-layout-strata from master. Follow its CLAUDE.md: LF only, US English, `filename-§N` citations, version ripple. Every later WS item adds a ruling paragraph under the entry this item opens and never bumps the version or date.

EDITS
1. standards/STANDARDS.md line 1: `# Ka0s WoW Addon Standard (v2.87.0, 2026-10-23)` becomes `# Ka0s WoW Addon Standard (v2.88.0, 2026-10-24)`.
2. Move the current entry. In standards/STANDARDS.md `## Changelog` (heading at line 98), the bullet that starts `- **v2.87.0 (2026-10-23):**` (line 100) runs through its closing `Minor.` line, which is just above `Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).`. Cut it and paste it verbatim into standards/CHANGELOG.md, directly under the intro paragraph (line 3) and above the `- **v2.86.0 (2026-10-22):**` bullet, with one blank line on each side. Change nothing in it.
3. In its place in STANDARDS.md, write the new entry:
   `- **v2.88.0 (2026-10-24):** **Key bindings in a category of their own, a Keybindings tab in every windowed addon's settings, and one frame-layering model.** The rulings below come from the collection run that gave each windowed addon its own section in the client's Keybindings page and an in-panel Keybindings tab, and set one strata and frame-level model for every addon (Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks `docs/2026-10-24-KEYBINDS_LAYOUT_STRATA/`, items 015 and 030); each paragraph is one ruling and names its ripple.`
   Then a blank line, an indented line `  Version rippled to `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md` and `NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md`.`, a blank line and `  Minor.`. That copies the v2.87.0 entry's shape. Later items insert their numbered rulings `(1)`, `(2)`... between the intro and the `Version rippled` line.
4. The mirrors that scripts/check-standard.sh `check_version_stamps` reads:
   - README.md `## Status` (line 173): `**v2.87.0**` becomes `**v2.88.0**`;
   - standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md line 11: `current: **v2.87.0**, 2026-10-23)` becomes `current: **v2.88.0**, 2026-10-24)`;
   - standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md line 1: `(v2.87.0, 2026-10-23)` becomes `(v2.88.0, 2026-10-24)`;
   - CLAUDE.md line 172: `As of v2.87.0 the sets are:` becomes `As of v2.88.0 the sets are:`. The doc sets do not change in this run, so the sentence stays as it is.
5. Run `bash scripts/check-standard.sh`. It must exit 0, with version-stamps reporting `v2.88.0, 2026-10-24 restated in all four places`.

Commit `WS-00: Open v2.88.0 for the keybindings and frame-layering run` with the session trailers.

items.spec:
Design: KEYBINDINGS_RESEARCH.md §2 (how retail turns `category=` into a section; a `header` draws as a blank spacer) and §5.3 and §5.5; LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON.md XC-03 and U-16. Owner ruling (OWNER_SCOPE upfront answer 1): each addon gets its own top-level category named after the addon. Pending owner call CALL-03: the examples below use the recommended labels (BankLedger 'Toggle ledger window'; DpsRace 'Toggle race HUD', 'Toggle results window', 'Arm or cancel race'; DropWatcher 'Toggle drop feed'; LootHistory 'Toggle history browser'; MultiMeters, QuickComms and WhatGroup unchanged). If the owner rules differently, only the example strings change. Say so in the changelog paragraph. Branch feat/2026-10-24-keybinds-layout-strata. Do not bump the version.

EDITS in standards/standards/launcher.md, §6 (lines 116-148):
1. Line 120, the first bullet: replace `with `category="ADDONS"`, and with `header="<FOLDERUPPER>"` on the file's **first** `<Binding>` only` with `with `category="BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>"` on **every** `<Binding>` in the file and **no** `header` attribute on any`. The rest of the bullet and its three not-allowed sub-bullets stay.
2. The XML example (lines 126-128): `<Binding name="CLICK <Folder>Toggle<Window>:LeftButton" category="BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>"/>`.
3. Line 130, the paragraph under the example, becomes: an addon that already ships bindings gives **every** line the same `category` and lists the Show window binding **first**, so the addon's section in the client and its Keybindings tab (options-ui-§20) both open on it. Rewrite the reference-implementation sentence the same way: the addon whose secure dial headers already had `CLICK` bindings added a line, **first** in the file, naming a plain hidden button. Drop 'a last line'.
4. New bullet after that paragraph: **Why the category, and why no header (v2.88.0).** The retail Keybindings page groups bindings by `category` and titles each group with `_G[category]` when that is a string, otherwise with the raw attribute text (Blizzard `Blizzard_SettingsDefinitions_Frame/Keybindings.lua`, `GetBindingCategoryName`). A `header` inside a category draws as a blank spacer row, not a title (the same file's list build). `category="ADDONS"` put every Ka0s binding into one shared *AddOns* section, where each addon's header row was an empty line and its brand never showed. A category named for `BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>` gives each addon its own section, titled with its brand, and reuses a global every addon already writes and declares. The client stores a key against the binding's **name**, never its category, so the move unbinds no player's key. Custom categories appear after Blizzard's own, in addon load order, and the collection does not control that position.
5. The labels bullet (lines 132-136) becomes three sub-bullets:
   - `BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>` is the addon's brand name, `Ka0s <Name>` (launcher-§1). It is read from the addon's one brand constant, the one its launcher label reads, and is never retyped as a literal. It is **also the title of the addon's section** in the client's Keybindings page. It **MUST** be assigned at the module's file scope, never lazily, because the client reads it when `ADDON_LOADED` fires for an addon with bindings.
   - `BINDING_NAME_<command>` for every binding comes through `L` (localization). The Show window label is `Toggle <the window's own name>`, with no article and no brand, because the category already carries the brand. Examples: *Toggle ledger window*, *Toggle history browser*, *Toggle drop feed*. Any other binding is a verb phrase naming its action (*Arm or cancel race*, *Open Comms Dial 1*).
   - **One bindings table.** The addon declares its bindings once, `NS.BINDINGS = { { command = "CLICK <Folder>Toggle<Window>:LeftButton", tooltip = L["..."] }, ... }`, in `Bindings.xml` order, in the module that creates the Show window button. The Keybindings tab (options-ui-§20) and the suite both read it.
   Keep the closing sentence about `rawset`.
6. Line 138 (No default key): the last sentence becomes 'The player chooses in the client's Options → Keybindings → `Ka0s <Name>`, or in the addon's own General → Keybindings tab (options-ui-§20).'
7. Line 141 (Documented): 'The README's `## Usage` names the binding and both places to set it: Options → Keybindings → `Ka0s <Name>`, and General → Keybindings in the addon's settings. `docs/settings-panel.md`'s launcher row lists it beside the *Show window* entry, and its General page lists the Keybindings tab.'
8. The rejection (lines 142-146): keep the three sub-bullets and add a paragraph after them. The rejection covers `Bindings.xml` and its `BINDING_*` globals, and it **stands**: both stay per addon, and no library writes a `BINDING_*` global. It did not cover the **settings-panel key editor**, which is a library surface from `LibKa0s v1.77.0` (`O.KeybindingsTab`, options-ui-§20). Capture, two-slot semantics, conflicts, combat and sync are high-content and identical in every addon that owes the binding, which is the shape library-stack-§7 promotes.
9. Line 147 (Re-check): add **The re-check trigger fired (v2.88.0).** Two owing addons ship more than one binding, so the deferred kit check is adopted. It is `Kit.assertBindingsXml(path, { category = "BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>", commands = NS.BINDINGS, brand = <brand constant> })` in the shared kit from `LibKa0s v1.77.0`. It asserts: the category on every `<Binding>`; no `header` and no `default`; the `name`s equal `NS.BINDINGS` in order; a `BINDING_NAME_` label for each; and `_G[category]` equal to the brand. The kit's `tests/_kit/mock_bindings.lua` is the binding model a suite loads (`GetBindingKey` with two slots, `GetBindingAction`, a `SetBinding` and `SaveBindings` that refuse in combat and fire `UPDATE_BINDINGS`, `GetCurrentBindingSet`/`LoadBindings`, `GetBindingName`/`GetBindingText`). An owing addon's binding test calls the check. `tests/test_disabled.lua` step 8 still covers the press (slash-commands-§7). Keep the existing trigger sentence above it as history.
10. Line 148 (Commencement): add 'The v2.88.0 shape (category, no header, labels, `NS.BINDINGS`, the kit check) commences at each owing addon's next release. The XML change and the rewrite of its shape test land in one commit, because the old test asserts `category="ADDONS"`.'

RIPPLE
11. standards/standards/anti-patterns.md line 125 (#96): before the closing citation parenthesis, append '; and, from v2.88.0, a `category` other than `BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>` on any `<Binding>`, a `header` attribute, a category global that is not the brand constant or is assigned lazily, or a binding label that repeats the brand'.
12. AUDIT.md lines 663-678 (the Show window key binding check). Item 1 becomes: a root `Bindings.xml` holds a `CLICK <button>:LeftButton` line with no `default` attribute and no Lua, with `category="BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>"` on **every** `<Binding>` and no `header` attribute (from the addon's first release after v2.88.0; before it, `category="ADDONS"` with `header` on the first line only was the shape), and with the Show window line first. Item 3 adds: the header is assigned at file scope from the brand constant, the labels follow launcher-§6's pattern, and `NS.BINDINGS` lists the file's names in order. Item 5 adds: the README names both places to set the key. Add item 6: the addon's binding test calls `Kit.assertBindingsXml` (from its first re-vendor of `LibKa0s v1.77.0`). Keep the closing paragraph, and add that a category still `ADDONS` after the addon's first release past v2.88.0 is #96.
13. standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md `### Bindings.xml and the Show window button (launcher-§6)` (lines 751-808):
   - line 757: '(the player picks the key in Options → Keybindings → `Ka0s <Name>`, or in the addon's General → Keybindings tab)';
   - the XML line (763): the new shape, with the comment adding 'every line carries this category; no header';
   - the Lua snippet: `BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER> = NS.BRAND` with the comment '-- the brand constant (launcher-§1), and the section title in Options → Keybindings', plus a `NS.BINDINGS = { { command = ("CLICK %s:LeftButton"):format(W.TOGGLE_BUTTON), tooltip = NS.L["Shows or hides the <window>."] } }` line with the comment '-- in Bindings.xml order; the Keybindings tab and the suite read it (launcher-§6, options-ui-§20)';
   - the closing paragraph (803-808): the README path becomes both places as in edit 7, and add that the binding test calls `Kit.assertBindingsXml`;
   - line 1627, hard rule 18a: `(`header` on the first `<Binding>` only, `category="ADDONS"`, **no `default`**)` becomes `(`category="BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>"` on every `<Binding>`, no `header`, **no `default`**)`, and add that the labels are 'Toggle <window>' with no brand and are listed in `NS.BINDINGS`;
   - line 1726, the Definition of done checkbox: add 'with `category="BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>"` and no `header`, the labels in `NS.BINDINGS`, and `Kit.assertBindingsXml` in the suite'.
14. NEW_ADDON.md line 246: '...a root `Bindings.xml` `CLICK` line in the addon's own category, the button, `NS.BINDINGS` and the General page's Keybindings tab (options-ui-§20), from the context pack.'
15. standards/STANDARDS.md line 63 (launcher blurb), the Show window clause: after 'a `CLICK` binding in a root `Bindings.xml`' insert ', in a Keybindings category of the addon's own named for its brand, with no header,'.
16. The v2.88.0 changelog entry: add ruling **(1) launcher-§6 and anti-pattern #96: each windowed addon's bindings in a category of its own.** **The finding.** The collection owner asked for proper names and categories in the client's Keybindings page, with the category named for the addon (OWNER_SCOPE 015, upfront answer 1). `category="ADDONS"` merged every Ka0s binding into one section, and the `header` drew as a blank row (Keybindings.lua, 12.1.5 source, KEYBINDINGS_RESEARCH §2). **The ruling.** The category, no header, file-scope brand header, the label pattern, `NS.BINDINGS`, the split rejection and the adopted kit check. The labels follow the recommended answer to the pending owner call CALL-03. **The ripple.** anti-patterns #96, AUDIT.md, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md, NEW_ADDON.md, the launcher index blurb, and the LibKa0s kit (`mock_bindings.lua`, `Kit.assertBindingsXml`, `LibKa0s v1.77.0`).

After the edits, `git grep -n 'category="ADDONS"\|Key Bindings → AddOns' -- '*.md'` outside harvests/, docs/audits/, docs/reviews/, standards/_raw/ and standards/CHANGELOG.md may return only the new 'before it ... was the shape' history clause in AUDIT.md. Run `bash scripts/check-standard.sh` (exit 0). Commit `WS-01: launcher-§6 per-addon binding category, labels and kit check`.

items.title: options-ui-§20 The Keybindings tab (U-03, XC-01/02/03): last General tab, library-drawn two-slot editor over the client's bindings; §13 host-tab bullet; anti-pattern #98; AUDIT.md check (k); pack, index blurbs, executive summary
items.spec:
Design: KEYBINDINGS_RESEARCH.md §3 (API, combat and taint, Blizzard parity, syncing with the set in force), §5.1 (the library surface), §5.4 and §5.5; LAYOUT_CROSS_ADDON.md XC-01, XC-02, XC-03, U-03. CALL-02 ('Master alpha' to 'Master opacity') is item 020's and is NOT touched here. Branch feat/2026-10-24-keybinds-layout-strata. Do not bump the version.

The LibKa0s surface this rule names, which the LibKa0s M1 items MUST match exactly: `O.KeybindingsTab(spec)` and `O.KeybindRows(ctx, spec, parent)` on the `LibKa0s-Options-1.0` instance, in a new file `OptionsKeybinds.lua`, from `LibKa0s v1.77.0`. `spec.bindings` = `{ { command, tooltip }, ... }`. `spec.key` defaults to "Keybindings". `spec.before` defaults to nil (last). `spec.intro` is an optional addon line drawn UNDER the library's fixed shared sentence and never replaces it.

1. standards/standards/options-ui.md: append at end of file (after §19, line 474) `### 20. The Keybindings tab (MUST, for an addon that ships launcher-§6 bindings)`, written in the file's voice with these rules:
   - **Who.** An addon whose `Bindings.xml` ships any binding (launcher-§6; the windowed addons in `ADDONS.md`'s *Show window* column) lets the player set those keys from its own settings. Both surfaces read and write the client's one store, so a key set in either shows in the other.
   - **Where (XC-01).** The **last** tab of the General page, labelled exactly `Keybindings`. It is a host tab (§13): drawn through `O.RenderTabbedSchema`'s `opts.tabs` with no `before`, so the library places it after every schema group. On a General page the host draws itself, it is the last entry of that strip, through `O.KeybindRows`. `Master controls` stays first (§15). A one-row Keybindings tab is legal.
   - **Drawn by the library.** `O.KeybindingsTab(spec)` (from `LibKa0s v1.77.0`), with `spec.bindings = NS.BINDINGS` (launcher-§6), so the rows follow `Bindings.xml`, which lists the Show window binding first. A hand-built key editor beside it is #47. AceGUI's `Keybinding` widget **MUST NOT** be used, for these reasons: Escape clears instead of cancelling; it has one slot, no META and no mouse button past 5; it has no binding semantics; its prompt is English-only; and its message frame is a toplevel `FULLSCREEN_DIALOG` frame at level 1000 (frame-layering-§1 keeps that tier for popups).
   - **A row.** The label is `GetBindingName(command)`, the exact `BINDING_NAME_` text the client's page shows, never a second label. It has **two** key slots, because the client keeps two per action and a single slot would hide a key set on the client's page. It has a Clear button and the row's tooltip.
   - **The intro (XC-02).** The tab opens with the library's fixed sentence, identical in every addon: *Key bindings are saved by the game, not in your profile. Defaults and Reset all settings leave them alone.* A host **MUST NOT** replace it. It **MAY** add one line under it (`spec.intro`) where a binding needs explaining, for example a dial whose key follows its place in a list.
   - **Under the rows.** One line names the set in force, *Saved for: all characters* or *Saved for: this character only*, followed by *(Options → Keybindings → Character Specific Keybindings)*. One line gives the last outcome, in the client's own strings: `KEY_BOUND`; `KEY_UNBOUND_ERROR` naming the action that lost its key; or *Key bindings can be changed after combat.*
   - **Behaves as the client's page does.** Left-click a slot to listen, and click again to cancel. Escape cancels. Right-click clears that slot. Mouse buttons 3-31 and the wheel can be captured. A modifier alone, `BUTTON1` and `BUTTON2` are ignored. Modifiers go in ALT-CTRL-SHIFT-META order. Taking a key from another action takes it without asking, as the client does, and the outcome line names the action that lost it.
   - **The client's store, the set in force.** The tab writes with `SetBinding` and saves with `SaveBindings(GetCurrentBindingSet())` right after each change. It **MUST NOT** keep a key in SavedVariables or a profile, so a profile copy, a reset or an import never carries one. It **MUST NOT** offer its own account/character switch: switching from character to account deletes the character set behind a Blizzard confirmation, and that stays Blizzard's.
   - **Sync.** It repaints on `UPDATE_BINDINGS`, registered only while a row is on screen and debounced to one repaint per frame, and it re-reads on the page's `OnShow`. It never caches a key.
   - **Combat.** No key is bound, cleared or saved in combat. Every write is refused under §2's lock, and a capture in progress is canceled at `PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED`.
   - **It never drives Blizzard's settings window.** It never touches `SettingsPanel` (no Commit, no Close, no `HideUIPanel`), `Settings.SelectCharacterBindings`/`SelectAccountBindings`, `KeybindListener` or the client's binding row template. The panel's own save on hide stays Blizzard's (§2, anti-pattern #88's reasoning).
   - **Resets do not reach keys (XC-02).** Bindings are client state, not schema rows. Page Defaults, *Reset all settings* (§12) and the schema CLI never touch them. The General page's header Defaults tooltip **SHOULD** end with *Key bindings are not changed.*
   - **Degradation.** Where the client lacks the binding API, the tab draws one text row pointing at Options → Keybindings. The options stub answers both members (§1; `Kit.assertSurfaceParity`).
   - **Testing (MUST).** The addon's suite pins four things: the General strip ends in `Keybindings`; the rows equal `NS.BINDINGS` in order; the labels shown equal the `BINDING_NAME_` globals; and a key bound through the tab is returned by `GetBindingKey` (the kit's `mock_bindings.lua`). The capture, slot, conflict, combat, sync and never-touches-SettingsPanel cases belong to the library's suite, and the addon **MUST NOT** duplicate them (testing-§8).
   - **Why (v2.88.0).** The owner asked for the keys in General → Keybindings, following and syncing with the client's global or character-specific set (OWNER_SCOPE 015). One addon added an in-panel key box on 2026-10-20 and retired it on 2026-10-21. This section **supersedes that retirement**: the editor returns as one library surface, so a later audit does not read it as a regression.
   - **Commencement.** Each owing addon's next release on `LibKa0s v1.77.0` or later. A missing tab or a misbehaving editor is anti-pattern #98.
2. options-ui.md §13 (bullets at lines 333-343): add a bullet after 'One tab per section, always.': **A host tab** is a tab drawn through `opts.tabs` for content that no schema row can declare. It sits in the same strip under the same session-state rule, and the page's Defaults does not reach it because it holds no rows. The Keybindings tab (§20) is one.
3. standards/standards/anti-patterns.md: append `98. **A key editor that is not the client's, or a windowed addon without one** — ...` listing: writes, clears or saves a key in combat; keeps a key in SavedVariables or a profile; offers its own account/character switch; closes, commits or hides Blizzard's settings window; reuses `KeybindListener` or the client's binding row template; uses AceGUI's `Keybinding` widget; shows one slot where the client keeps two; labels a row with anything but `GetBindingName`; is hand-built beside `O.KeybindingsTab`; replaces the shared intro sentence; and an addon that ships launcher-§6 bindings with no Keybindings tab, or with one that is not the General page's last (`options-ui-§20`, `launcher-§6`). Then STANDARDS.md line 80: `(#1–#97)` becomes `(#1–#98)`.
4. AUDIT.md: line 903 'Ten checks.' becomes 'Eleven checks.'. Insert after the (j) block (it starts at line 1082) and before '**File the strip and the tab rules as one root with dependents**' (line 1106): **(k) The Keybindings tab (options-ui-§20, v2.88.0).** For an addon with a root `Bindings.xml`: the General page's last tab is `Keybindings`, drawn by `O.KeybindingsTab`/`O.KeybindRows` (grep the settings files); it passes `NS.BINDINGS`; there is no `AceGUI:Create("Keybinding")`, `SetBinding`, `SaveBindings` or `KeybindListener` in the addon's own code (`grep -rnE 'Create\("Keybinding"\)|SetBinding\(|SaveBindings|KeybindListener' --include='*.lua' . | grep -v -e /libs/ -e /tests/_kit/`; a hit outside a secure override-binding path the addon documents is #98); and the General Defaults tooltip ends with 'Key bindings are not changed.' (SHOULD). The tab is owed from the addon's first release on `LibKa0s v1.77.0` or later; before that tag it is a re-vendor item.
5. standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md: in hard rule 8b (lines 1606-1612), add a bullet: an addon with bindings ends its General page with the `Keybindings` host tab drawn by `O.KeybindingsTab({ bindings = NS.BINDINGS })`; keys stay the client's, saved to the set in force; the intro is the library's; resets never reach keys (options-ui-§20). In the Definition of done, after line 1726, add a checkbox with the same substance. In the `settings/OptionsSetup.lua` snippet's degradation stub, if it enumerates instance members (check around lines 611-750), add `KeybindingsTab` and `KeybindRows`.
6. standards/STANDARDS.md line 60 (options-ui blurb): append '; and, for an addon with key bindings, the General page's last tab, **Keybindings**, the library's two-slot editor over the client's own bindings, saved to the set in force, never in a profile, refused in combat (options-ui-§20)'.
7. standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md line 22 (**One panel, contents included**): add one sentence: a windowed addon's General page ends in a library-drawn **Keybindings** tab that edits the client's own bindings (options-ui-§20).
8. The v2.88.0 changelog entry: add ruling **(2) options-ui-§20 and anti-pattern #98: the Keybindings tab.** It has The finding (OWNER_SCOPE 015; XC-01/02/03), The ruling, the supersession of the 2026-10-21 key-box retirement, and The ripple (§13 host tab, #98, AUDIT.md (k), NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md, the index blurb, EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md, and `LibKa0s v1.77.0`'s `OptionsKeybinds.lua`).

Run `bash scripts/check-standard.sh` (exit 0; anti-patterns '#1–#98 contiguous'). Commit `WS-02: options-ui-§20 Keybindings tab and anti-pattern #98`.

One kit revision for the whole release: Kit.VERSION 41 -> 42 (`testkit/framework.lua:20`). Edit testkit/ only, then `cp -r testkit/. tests/_kit/` (releasing.md step 2). All new files CRLF (the .gitattributes pin; test_eol gates it), ASCII in strings.

A. testkit/mock_bindings.lua (new; OPT-IN installer, the testkit/mock_ids.lua:1-39 pattern: NOT loaded by mock_base.lua, which is at 1464 lines against its 1490 re-check trigger). Shape: `return function(M, opts) ... return M end`, used as `dofile("tests/_kit/mock_bindings.lua")(M)` on a finished mock. Fills only keys still missing on M (a consumer's own fixture wins), except the seams prefixed `__binding`. Model, ported from QuickComms `tests/wow_mock.lua:908-940`:
  - storage per binding set: `M.__bindingSets = { [1] = {actions={}, keys={}}, [2] = {...} }`, live set `M.__bindingSet` (default 1). `keys[command]` is an ARRAY in bind order; `actions[key] = command`.
  - `GetBindingKey(command)` -> every key in order (unpack), nil when none. `GetBindingAction(key)` -> command or "".
  - `SetBinding(key, command)`: when `M.InCombatLockdown()` is true it appends `{ key, command }` to `M.__bindingRefusals` and returns false. When `M.__bindingFailNext == key` it clears that seam and returns false (a refused bind, for restore tests). Otherwise command nil unbinds the key; a command takes the key from its previous action (removed from that action's array) and appends it to the command's array; appends to `M.__bindingWrites`; then, unless `M.__bindingsFireOnSet == false`, fires `M.__fire("UPDATE_BINDINGS")` (mock_record.lua:580, live registrations only) and increments `M.__bindingFires`. Returns true.
  - `SaveBindings(set)`: refused in combat (recorded in `M.__bindingRefusals` as `{ save = set }`, returns nothing); else copies the live tables into `M.__bindingSets[set]`, appends `set` to `M.__savedBindingSets`, fires UPDATE_BINDINGS.
  - `GetCurrentBindingSet()` -> `M.__bindingSet`. `LoadBindings(set)`: makes `set` live (its saved tables), sets `M.__bindingSet = set`, fires UPDATE_BINDINGS.
  - `GetBindingText(key)` -> key (identity). `GetBindingName(command)` -> `M["BINDING_NAME_"..command]` or `_G[...]`, else command (BindingUtil.lua:142-149's fallback).
  - Constants filled if missing: `NOT_BOUND = "Not Bound"`, `KEY_BOUND = "Key Bound Successfully"`, `KEY_UNBOUND_ERROR = "|cffff0000%s Function is Now Unbound!|r"`, `ACCOUNT_BINDINGS = 1`, `CHARACTER_BINDINGS = 2`, and `M.Enum.BindingSet = { Default = 0, Account = 1, Character = 2 }` merged into an existing `M.Enum` without replacing it.
  - Modifier state: `IsAltKeyDown`, `IsControlKeyDown`, `IsShiftKeyDown`, `IsMetaKeyDown` read `M.__modifiers`; `M.setModifiers{ alt=, ctrl=, shift=, meta= }` sets it (all false by default).
  - Helpers: `M.bindKey(key, command)` seeds without firing or recording; `M.clearBindings()` empties both sets and the logs.
  - `opts.clientChordHelpers = true` also installs faithful `GetConvertedKeyOrButton` (LeftButton->BUTTON1, RightButton->BUTTON2, MiddleButton->BUTTON3, ButtonN->BUTTONN, else the key), `IsKeyPressIgnoredForBinding` (LSHIFT RSHIFT LCTRL RCTRL LALT RALT LMETA RMETA UNKNOWN BUTTON1 BUTTON2) and `CreateKeyChordStringUsingMetaKeyState(key)` (ALT-CTRL-SHIFT-META- prefix order, BindingUtil.lua:116-134); by default they are absent so a suite exercises the library's bundled fallback.
B. testkit/mock_layers.lua (new; OPT-IN installer `dofile("tests/_kit/mock_layers.lua")(M)` returning a `restore` function). Wraps `M.CreateFrame` so every frame created after install gets recorded layer methods (rawset on the frame; document that a suite spying by rawset on such a frame restores by re-assigning the previous function, not nil, because the base's `rawset nil to restore` idiom, mock_base.lua:170-172, would erase the recorder): `SetFrameStrata/GetFrameStrata` (own value, else the parent chain's, else "MEDIUM"), `SetFixedFrameStrata/HasFixedFrameStrata`, `SetFrameLevel/GetFrameLevel` (own explicit value, else parent level + 1, root 0), `SetFixedFrameLevel/HasFixedFrameLevel`, `SetToplevel/IsToplevel`, `SetClampedToScreen/IsClampedToScreen`, `Raise`/`Lower` (counted in `__raised`/`__lowered`), `SetIgnoreParentAlpha/IsIgnoringParentAlpha`, and `SetParent/GetParent` reading and writing `__parent` (mock_base.lua:1153) where `SetParent` drops an explicit level (the client re-derives it, STRATA_MODEL §1 / KIC-Z06). Survey `M.__layers(frame)` -> `{ strata, level, toplevel, clamped, fixedStrata, ignoreParentAlpha, raised }`. Strata values are validated against the eight client names; an unknown one raises naming itself.
C. testkit/bindings_xml.lua (new; loaded by framework.lua beside latch.lua at :242 as `dofile(kitFolder() .. "bindings_xml.lua")(Kit)`), installing `Kit.assertBindingsXml(path, opts)`; Kit.expose (:247-266) adds `t.assertBindingsXml = Kit.assertBindingsXml`. opts: `category` (required string, e.g. "BINDING_HEADER_BANKLEDGER"), `commands` (required array, file order), `brand` (required string), `globals` (table to read globals from, default _G), `labels` (optional map command -> expected BINDING_NAME_ text). It reads the file, parses every `<Binding .../>` or `<Binding ...>` element's attributes, and fails (Kit.fail, caller's line, message naming the file and `launcher-§6`) unless: there is at least one Binding; every Binding's `category` equals opts.category; no Binding has `header=` or `default=`; the names equal opts.commands in order; each `globals["BINDING_NAME_"..name]` is a non-empty string (and equals labels[name] when given); `globals[opts.category] == opts.brand`. Returns the parsed list `{ { name=, category= }, ... }`.
D. testkit/README.md file table (rows for the three files, kit revision 42) and the "A copy that leaves out ..." sentence (:46-48) gains bindings_xml.lua. Not mock_bindings/mock_layers there: they are opt-in, like mock_ids.lua.

Design: STRATA_MODEL.md §6.2 (drag handle ties with the content it edits, fades with the host's alpha; hosts re-level it after its marks exist) and §7 row LK-02 (70%). Consumers in M2 (ZS items): AbsorbTracker ABS-Z04 (level 5) and ABS-Z06, AuraMaster handle L+50 and AUR-Z12, ConsumableMaster CON-Z08 and CON-Z10, KickCD KIC-Z07 (HUD_LEVEL + 39 expressed over each handle's parent), QuickComms QUI-Z11. Rules: frame-layering-§2 (edit chrome on top of its display, reachable, undimmed — XS-05) and §3 (relative levels, re-assert what moves — XS-15, XS-18).

FILE LibKa0s/WidgetsDragHandle.lua (DRAG_MINOR 4 -> 5 at :49; header note `Minor 5:`).
- Spec docblock above `lib.DragHandle` (:600-648) gains two fields:
  `level  number|nil  minor 5. The handle's frame level as an OFFSET over parent:GetFrameLevel(), applied at birth before the help and close marks are built, so the marks are born at handle + 1. nil keeps minor 4's implicit parent + 1.`
  `ignoreParentAlpha  boolean|nil  minor 5. true calls SetIgnoreParentAlpha(true) on the handle, so a display that fades its content (mouseover fade, a combat alpha) does not fade the strip a player must still find. The marks are the handle's children and follow it.`
- In lib.DragHandle (:649-675), right after the `handle and handle.SetHeight` guard (:654) and before dhBuildChrome: when `type(spec.level) == "number"`, set `handle:SetFrameLevel(base + spec.level)` where `base = dhNumber(spec, parent:GetFrameLevel(), 0)` (the existing secret-safe guard at :205; a non-number answer reads as 0); when `spec.ignoreParentAlpha == true` and `handle.SetIgnoreParentAlpha` is a function, call it with true.
- dhAttachMethods (:565) adds `handle:ApplyLevel()`: with a numeric spec.level it re-reads the parent's level through dhNumber, re-sets the handle to base + level, then sets `handle.help` and `handle.close` (when present) to the handle's level + 1 explicitly, and returns true; with no spec.level it changes nothing and returns false. Doc comment: a host calls it after it re-levels or re-parents the handle's parent (SetParent re-derives levels, XS-18), never in a memoized restyle only.
- Nothing else changes: default behavior is minor 4's byte for byte when neither field is passed.

TESTS FIRST: new tests/test_widgets_draghandle_layers.lua (keep tests/test_widgets_draghandle.lua at 813 lines out of the band), added to tests/run.lua beside test_widgets_draghandle_place, with mock_layers installed per case and the bench from tests/fixture_draghandle.lua:
- no level: the handle is parent + 1 and the marks handle + 1 (minor 4's shape pinned);
- level = 50 on a parent at 7: handle 57, help and close 58 at birth (assert they were born after the level write: record SetFrameLevel order);
- parent re-levelled to 20 then ApplyLevel(): handle 70, marks 71, returns true; ApplyLevel with no spec.level returns false and writes nothing;
- a secret / non-number parent level (spec.number guard) reads as 0;
- ignoreParentAlpha = true sets IsIgnoringParentAlpha; absent leaves it false; a frame without the method does not error;
- a handle with onClose and level builds both marks at handle + 1.

items.spec:
Design: STRATA_MODEL.md §6.2 (IdList suggestions on UIParent escape the combat cover over their page, BAN-S11) and §7 row LK-04 (45%, 'land only after an in-client check'). DECISION (lead's, recorded here): land it now and move the in-client check to a smoke test. Closing the list at combat start is safe whether or not the list is clickable over the cover: a pick made in combat is already refused by the write seam (O.__combatRefused), so closing loses nothing a player could have used, and AceGUI pullouts are already closed the same way. Rule: XS-10 / frame-layering-§4 (a transient popup closes on every path its opener closes).

  - The table first (§5): an addon with any explicit layering and no `NS.Constants.LAYERS` in `core/Constants.lua`; then `grep -nE 'SetFrameStrata\(\s*"' <files>` (a strata string at a call site) and `grep -nE 'SetFrameLevel\(\s*[0-9]' <files>` (an absolute level) should be empty; every `SetFrameLevel` argument names a `LAYERS.LEVEL` member. A frameless addon (no window, no HUD) calling `SetFrameStrata`/`SetFrameLevel`/`SetToplevel`/`Raise` at all is a finding.
  - Sibling-relative and captured levels (§3): `SetFrameLevel(x:GetFrameLevel() + n)` where `x` is not the frame's own parent or the band's named base (read the call, do not grep-and-file); a level captured once against a base that moves later (a pooled carrier, a raised parent); a level set before `SetParent` and not re-set after it.

  - Glow (§3): a `LibKa0s-Glow-1.0` `Start(...)` with no explicit small `frameLevel` (LibCustomGlow's default +8 leaps over the overlay rung).
  - Edit chrome (§2): a DragHandle/outline/grip that inherits a player strata below MEDIUM while mouse-enabled, ties with the content it edits, or fades with the display's alpha while clickable. From LibKa0s v1.77.0 the fix is the DragHandle `level` and `ignoreParentAlpha` spec fields (names as landed by LK-90), not a host re-level after construction.
  - Windows (§4): a frame that is `SetMovable(true)` (or carries a LibKa0s drag bar) with no `SetToplevel(true)`, outside the two §1 documented exceptions (secure fixed point; event-raised notice previewed from Settings), each of which needs a call-site comment and a `## Documented deviations` row; a window opened from another window in an equal or lower strata.

Each change bumps the minor of the files it touches once, and this block names each new minor as it lands. Still seventeen majors across forty files." Nothing else.
- Do NOT bump any minor, Kit.VERSION, README or releasing.md. Do not tag.

THE IN-RELEASE DOCUMENT RULE (record it in the commit body; every later LK item follows it): `tests/test_versioning.lua` derives `docs/api/<Major>/version-<key>-docs.md` from each major's live `lib.MODULES` and regenerates `members-<key>.json` (tools/gen-api-members.lua), so every commit's gate needs the doc and manifest for the CURRENT key. The release ships ONE new document per moved major (as Sim 2.3.5 did at v1.76.0). The first item that moves a major copies that major's v1.76.0 Current doc to the new key (Status Current, Supersedes the v1.76.0 key, a `What changed at this version` section), marks the v1.76.0 doc Superseded with a `Moving to ...` section, adds the docs/api/README.md row and runs `lua tools/gen-api-members.lua`. A later item that moves the same major again `git mv`s THAT doc to the newer key (deleting the stale generated manifest, then regenerating), edits its What-changed section, the superseded doc's `Superseded by`/`Moving to` target and the README row, so no intermediate key ships a document. v1.76.0 Current docs (verified): Core 11, DebugLog 20.3.1, Perf 15.1.1.8, Sim 2.3.5, Widgets 14.1.4.3.2, Options 29.2.34.2.5.9.1.7.4.2.1, testkit 41.

FILE LibKa0s/WidgetsDragHandle.lua (675 lines; DRAG_MINOR 4 -> 5 at :49; `Minor 5:` header note).
- Spec docblock above `lib.DragHandle` (:600-648) gains:
  `level  number|nil  minor 5. The handle's frame level as an OFFSET over parent:GetFrameLevel(), applied at birth before the help and close marks are built, so the marks are born at handle + 1. nil keeps minor 4's implicit parent + 1.`
  `ignoreParentAlpha  boolean|nil  minor 5. true calls SetIgnoreParentAlpha(true) on the handle, so a display that fades its content does not fade the strip a player must find. The marks are its children and follow it.`
- In lib.DragHandle (:649-675), right after the `handle and handle.SetHeight` guard (:654) and before `dhBuildChrome` (:656): when `type(spec.level) == "number"`, `handle:SetFrameLevel(base + spec.level)` with `base = dhNumber(spec, parent:GetFrameLevel(), 0)` (the secret-safe guard, :205; a non-number answer reads 0); when `spec.ignoreParentAlpha == true` and `handle.SetIgnoreParentAlpha` is a function, call it with true. The marks are built later in the function (`dhBuildHelp`/`dhBuildClose` at :667-668), so they are born over the new level.
- dhAttachMethods (:565) adds `handle:ApplyLevel()`: with numeric spec.level, re-read the parent's level through dhNumber, set the handle to base + level, then set `handle.help` and `handle.close` (when present) to the handle's level + 1 explicitly; return true. With no spec.level, write nothing and return false. Doc: a host calls it after it re-levels or re-parents the handle's parent (SetParent re-derives levels, XS-18), never only in a memoized restyle.
- Default behavior is minor 4's when neither field is passed.

- level = 50 on a parent at 7: handle 57, help and close 58 at birth (record SetFrameLevel order: the handle's write precedes the marks' creation);
- parent re-levelled to 20 then ApplyLevel(): handle 70, marks 71, returns true; with no spec.level returns false and writes nothing;
- a secret / non-number parent level reads as 0;
- ignoreParentAlpha = true sets IsIgnoringParentAlpha; absent leaves it false; a frame without the method does not error;
- onClose plus level builds both marks at handle + 1.
